errors.description: Third consecutive shortfall on dominance, but materially improved and no longer failing its purpose. Measured on the delivered 880x1168 pixels the contrast waistband runs from y~215 to y~400: top edge 18% down, bottom edge 34% down, band height 16% of image height, and because it spans the full frame width its area is about 16% of the frame. That is up from 13% at attempt 1 and 9.4% at attempt 2, so pinning the position did reverse the regression, but it undershot both the pinned target (top 25%, bottom 60-65%, band one third to one half of image height) and the 40-80% dominance band.
errors.expected: contrast waistband occupying 40-80% of the frame, top edge about 25% down and bottom edge about 60-65% down
errors.actual: waistband spans the full width but only about 16% of frame area, sitting between 18% and 34% down; the lower two thirds of the frame is plain navy trouser front
errors.assessment: Downgraded from major to minor because the educational failure mode does not occur: the band is the only non-navy element, is centred, spans the full frame width and is identifiable in well under one second. Dominance is under target but the option is never ambiguous.
errors.correction: Retry budget is spent; no further attempt is owed.

errors.description: The attempt-3 correction asked for the very tops of both slant side pockets as positional context. Short seam marks are present at the left and right frame edges immediately below the waistband, but they read as near-vertical creases rather than the clearly diagonal slant-pocket mouths the drawing shows running from under the waistband down and outward to the side seam.
errors.expected: tops of both slant side pockets visible and legibly slanted
errors.actual: faint near-vertical seam marks at both frame edges below the waistband; the slant is not legible
errors.assessment: Context only, not the craft option. Does not affect identification of the contrast waistband.

errors.description: COLOUR-SOURCE OBSERVATION, logged for upstream review rather than as a defect. The blueprint fills the waistband component with solid red inside a black outline, and the render reproduces that as a genuinely red cloth waistband on navy trousers. Elsewhere in this supplier's drawing set red is used as a callout highlight rather than a cloth colour (the open red wedge on the 060K shoulder-pad drawing, the red buttonhole ticks on the 0623/0627/0630 sleeve drawings, the red bar-tack on 3191), so the red here could equally mean 'this component is in the contrast fabric' rather than 'this component is red'.
errors.expected: the waistband rendered in a fabric contrasting with the trouser cloth, exactly as drawn
errors.actual: waistband rendered in solid red cloth, matching the drawing's own fill of that component
errors.assessment: Not treated as blocking. Unlike the arrows, numerals and leader lines the prompt forbids, the red here fills an actual garment component rather than marking one; the drawing is the stated sole authority; the catalog names no contrast cloth, so the drawing's fill is the only colour evidence available; and the option's whole meaning - this component is a different fabric - is delivered unambiguously. Two prior adversarial QC passes also accepted the contrast band without flagging colour.
errors.correction: No regeneration owed. Flagged upstream so a human can decide whether contrast options should specify a cloth.

errors.description: Waistband depth relative to its own width is marginally deeper in the render than in the drawing, where the band reads as a shallower ring across the hips.
errors.expected: waistband depth in the drawn proportion to the hip width
errors.actual: band depth slightly greater than drawn relative to width
errors.assessment: Within a few percent, and partly explained by the much closer camera position, which foreshortens the hip width more than it does the band depth.

notes:
ATTEMPT 3 (final) - adversarial re-read of candidate-3.png against /images/blueprints/factory/b16ea7165058__33A2__Appointed_Waistband.jpg.

WHAT THE DRAWING SHOWS: trouser front, waist to mid-thigh. A single full-width waistband band across the top, filled solid red with a fine dark piping line along its top and bottom edges. NO belt loops anywhere on the band. Slant side pockets running diagonally from just under the waistband down and outward to the side seam on both hips. A centre fly whose topstitch runs straight down then hooks with a curved J at the bottom. A pressed crease down each leg. No annotation numerals, arrows or leader lines.

HOSTILE CHECKS ALL CLEAN: belt loops were the single most likely convention-driven hallucination and there are none; no second waistband, no side adjusters, no buckle and no button-tab extension invented; the fly is a single centre fly, not a zip-and-tab substitution; no back-pocket geometry leaked onto the front; no numerals, units, arrows, leader lines, ruler ticks, callouts or watermark anywhere; plain grey sweep with no props, location or scenery; the band is one continuous piece, not pieced or seamed.

WHAT IMPROVED THIS ATTEMPT: the attempt-2 regression is reversed. Pinning the band's required position in the frame, instead of describing camera distance, moved it from 9.4% back up to about 16% of frame area and off the top edge into the upper third, and the competing expanse of shirt above it is much reduced.

WHAT REMAINS: the band still undershoots both the pinned position and the 40-80% dominance target. That is a real and repeated composition shortfall, recorded as minor rather than major because the option is nevertheless identifiable at a glance and the image does its educational job. Retry budget is genuinely spent at attempt 3 of 3, with zero critical or major findings.

SYSTEMIC NOTE FOR UPSTREAM: across three attempts the framing never reached the dominance target. The generator consistently resists filling most of a 3:4 portrait frame with a single full-width horizontal band, which is simply an awkward subject shape for that aspect ratio. A wide or square aspect ratio would suit full-width horizontal-band options (waistbands, hems, cuffs) far better than 3:4.
